blocks.content: The Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989 and the Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 set out the basic rules every driver must follow.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Adhere strictly to standard driving rules to ensure overall road safety and legal compliance.
Recognize critical traffic situations and locations where overtaking is legally prohibited.
Maintain continuous awareness of driver duties required at all times while operating a vehicle.

blocks.content: Keep Left: Always drive as close to the left side of the road as possible. Allow traffic coming from the opposite direction to pass on your right.
Turning Left: When turning left, drive close to the left side of the road you are leaving and the road you are entering.
Turning Right: When turning right, move towards the centre of the road, then turn and keep to the left side of the road you enter.
Overtaking: Overtake from the RIGHT side only. Do not overtake from the left except when the vehicle ahead is turning right and there is space on the left.
Lane Discipline: Drive within your lane. Change lanes only after giving a proper signal. Do not weave between lanes.
Right of Way: At a STOP sign — stop completely before the stop line. At a GIVE WAY sign — slow down and give way to traffic on the main road.
Pedestrian Crossing: Slow down before a pedestrian crossing. Give way to pedestrians crossing the road. Do not park near a pedestrian crossing.
Both Hands on Wheel: A driver must hold the steering wheel with both hands at all times except when signalling.

items: Competitive exams frequently test specific scenarios and road junctions where overtaking is legally banned.
Questions often cover statutory driver duties and mandatory compliance under the Motor Vehicles Act.
If overtaking may cause danger or inconvenience to other traffic
Near a bend, corner, hill, or any place where the road ahead is not clearly visible
When the driver behind you has already started to overtake you
When the driver ahead has not signalled that you may overtake
At a road intersection or junction
When a school bus is stopped and children are getting on/off
Maintain a good lookout and concentrate on the road
Avoid any activity that distracts attention (e.g. using mobile phone)
Take special care of pedestrians, cyclists, children, the elderly, and differently-abled persons
Ensure the vehicle does not block or cause inconvenience to other road users
Ensure your view is not blocked by passengers, animals, or load in the vehicle
Ensure all occupants wear seat belts
If a technical defect is found while driving, take the vehicle off the road immediately
